step1_analysis.description: A fully differential 3rd-order active low-pass filter used in the baseband section of a WCDMA receiver. It utilizes a Sallen-Key topology (A1/A2 with RC feedback) followed by a passive RC output stage to achieve a 1.92 MHz cutoff frequency for channel selection.

paper_reference.title: Full-CMOS 2-GHz WCDMA Direct Conversion Transmitter and Receiver

passband_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the active filter.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the non-inverting amplifier gain 1 + R6/R7. With R6=R7=10k, gain is 2 (6 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The baseband filter typically provides a fixed moderate gain, while variable gain is handled by cascaded VGA stages.

sky130_expected.calculation: fc = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(R9*R13*C2*C3)). With R=8.29k and C=10pF, fc is approximately 1.92 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: 1.92 MHz is the standard baseband cutoff frequency for WCDMA (half of the 3.84 Mcps chip rate).

stopband_attenuation.description: Filter attenuation at out-of-band frequencies (e.g., 10 MHz).

sky130_expected.calculation: A 3rd-order filter rolls off at -60 dB/decade. From 1.92 MHz to 10 MHz is ~0.7 decades, expecting ~40 dB attenuation relative to passband.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Crucial for rejecting adjacent channel interference (ACPR) in direct conversion receivers.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the AC frequency response (gain, cutoff frequency, stopband attenuation) and transient response of the differential Sallen-Key baseband filter.
